details.publicNotes:
Liquefieds result from unethical magical experiments that explored the possibility of artificially creating new forms of elementals.

The process to create a liquefied involves taking a humanoid and slowly infusing them with a water elemental, erasing the minds of both creatures. Though liquefieds weren't what the researchers initially hoped to create, they secured numerous unscrupulous patrons willing to pay handsomely for an army of liquefied guardians and soldiers. The survivors of this grisly process still wander the world today.

Liquefieds dwell in dark, damp areas, where they spend much of their time resting in the form of puddles. When unwitting prey steps on a liquefied, the liquefied rises and engulfs it. After a lengthy digestion process, it grows slightly in size. Over time, as a liquefied continues to eat and grow, it eventually splits into a pair of liquefieds. Although there are whispers of supermassive liquefieds lurking in unexplored caverns and consuming would-be spelunkers.

Water Has Memory

Liquefieds have long outlived both their creators and the original owners who tried to turn them into soldiers or guardians. In many cases, not only did they outlive them, but they were the direct causes of their deaths. Although liquefieds are nearly mindless, they do possess a hatred for those who try to restrain them and a hunter's patient cunning—and it's hard to avoid an enemy who can be lurking in any puddle, bath, or rain barrel.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 64/140/250 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning), shield, perception item, skill items (Athletics, Stealth)

Eligible Imbued Properties body, bane, charisma, constitution, dexterity, energy resistant (vitality), sensory (darkvision), strength, sturdy, throwing, time, water, wild, wisdom

description.value: In its resting state, a liquefied's body is an immobile puddle, and other creatures can freely enter its space. A liquefied can temporarily solidify through applied pressure or quick impacts onto it. At the end of the liquefied's turn, if it was not exposed to any sources of pressure or movement since the end of its previous turn, such as taking force or physical damage or moving (either with an action or forced movement), it reverts to an immobile puddle.

Trigger A melee attack that deals force or physical damage critically hits the liquefied

Effect The liquefied returns the momentum back to the attacker, attempting a fist Strike against it and adding any additional damage from Stored Momentum. This Strike neither applies nor counts toward the liquefied's multiple attack penalty.

The liquefied's body's dramatic reaction to sudden impacts is lessened when the attacker's movements are slowed. Slowed creatures who Strike the liquefied with a melee attack ignore its resistance to bludgeoning and don't trigger its Bounce Back reaction.

A liquefied retains some of the force from its enemy's attacks and uses it to empower its own Strikes. Each time the liquefied takes force or physical damage, it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to damage on its next fist Strike. This bonus is cumulative, to a maximum bonus of +8 damage. The bonus damage decreases by 2 for every action the liquefied takes on its turn before Striking.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-effects.Item.9Jp2ay7kyPcngogp]{Effect: Stored Momentum}

Trigger A Medium or smaller creature steps onto the liquefied's space

Requirements The liquefied is in its puddle form

Effect The liquefied attempts an Athletics check to pull the creature into its body. This functions as Swallow Whole against a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} creature, except it does not have the attack trait (@Damage[(2d10+2)[bludgeoning]] damage, Rupture 17).

The liquefied expands its body out into a 20-foot radius puddle. All creatures in the area take @Damage[5d6[bludgeoning]] damage and must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:26] save. The liquefied then gathers itself back up to occupy any 10-foot square within the radius.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is pushed up to 5 feet toward the outer edge of the puddle; this is forced movement.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature takes double damage and is pushed up to 10 feet.
